Harun-ur Rashid—For the Petitioner.

parties:
Nurul Islam (Md) ------- Petitioner
Vs
Bangladesh Milk Producers Co-operative Union Ltd ------- Opposite Party
full_judgment: 2. The opposite party as petitioner (hereinafter referred to as opposite party) filed an application under section 134(5) of the Co-operative Societies Ordinance, 1984, before the District Judge, Dhaka against the decision dated 12-9-1995 passed by Mr Md Benaul Islam, Appellate Officer and Joint Registrar, Co-operative Societies in Appeal Case No. 8 of 1995 affirming the award dated 12-6-95 given in Dispute Case No. 1 of 1995 (A-1), stating, inter alia, that the opposite party was registered on 15th day of November, 1965 under Co-operative Societies Act, 1940 in the name of Bangladesh Milk Producers Co-operative Union Limited having its head office at 139-140, Tejgaon Industrial Area, and factory in Section-7 under Police Station, Mirpur and is engaged in collecting milk and through processing milk, butter, ghee and cheese are produced and marketed for sale. The petitioner was appointed on 30-3-1976 as Junior Officer under the opposite party on the basis of his application dated 8-3-1976 and afterwards was promoted as Assistant Manager, Deputy Manager and lastly, as Manager on and from 24-6-1990. The opposite party on coming to know that the petitioner in collaboration with other employees appropriated huge amount of money by making various false statements in respect of milk and oil, appointed Mr Rabiul Islam to enquire into the matter who submitted his report on 12-4-93 to the General Manager, who by his order dated 15-4-93 transferred the petitioner to the head office and made him OSD. Being instructed by the General Manager, three officers, namely, Md Aminul Islam, Md Rabiul Islam and Md Sariful Islam submitted their preliminary report on 15-4-1993 on appropriation of milk of the said factory by the petitioner in collaboration with other employees by making false statements in respect of oil and milk. The petitioner was charge-sheeted on 19-4-93 with the allegations of committing theft of 4500 litres of oil and of appropriation of Taka 50,000 therefrom and also allegations of appropriation of boiler oil, theft of milk fat and powder milk. An enquiry committed comprising of three officers namely Mr Gobindra Shaha, Mr Abdul Khaleque and Mr Mostafa Kamal was formed to enquire into the allegations levelled in the charge-sheet. The enquiry committee submitted its report on 22-6-1993 before the Managing Committee finding appropriation of about Taka 80,000. The Managing Committee in its meeting dated 23-6-93 and 24-6-93 examined the enquiry report and after discussing the matter found the petitioner guilty and accordingly, dismissed him legally by a letter dated 27-6-1996. The petitioner by filing an application dated 22-7-93 to the Chairman Managing Committee prayed for reversal of the aforesaid order of dismissal. The Chairman of the Committee constituted a Dispute Settlement Board consisting of three members and directed them to submit a report on the basis of the enquiry report and the related documents. The Board submitted a report to the Chairman on 6-10-1993. The Managing Committee in its meeting dated 19-1-94 decided to impose minor penalty of termination instead of dismissal considering the age of the petitioner and the condition of his family members and also asked him to accept all service benefits. The petitioner again applied to the Chairman on 24-2-94 for re-consideration of the said decision and the Chairman again sent the matter to the Dispute Settlement Board on 26-2-94. The petitioner filed a dispute case being No. 5 of 1994 before the Co-operative Societies Bangladesh, Dhaka and the case was fixed for hearing on 2-11-94, 6-11-94 and 12-11-94. Since the petitioner refused to accept the termination order and the financial benefit before the dispute case was being heard the opposite party restored the previous order of dismissal by an order dated 6-11-1994. As a result the Dispute Case No. 5 of 1994 became infructuous. In the above circumstances, the petitioner filed a new dispute case before the Registrar, Co-operative Societies Bangladesh being No. 1 of 1995 (A-1). The Deputy Registrar (Extension) who heard the case by her order dated 12-6-1995 held that the dismissal order of the opposite party was illegal and unlawful and directed to reinstate him in his former post from the date of his dismissal.
